_comment: A WORKED EXAMPLE for the identifiers requirement, built from captured bytes by experiments/v3-3/build_ident_fixture.mjs. It exists because that row renders NO QUOTE: it says 'Your structured data publishes MPN' and shows the merchant nothing to be suspicious of, so a human reading rendered evidence cannot tell a real GS1 barcode from a number the store minted about itself. Eighteen false passes hid behind that in a sample whose full read had reported zero, and correcting them moved a published bound from 0.83% to 7.80%.
requirement: A product identifier is published in structured data
why_it_matters: The row's promise is that a machine buyer can match this exact product to an EXTERNAL catalogue. A store-local id cannot do that — it resolves inside one shop and nowhere else — which is why the requirement names the SKU as explicitly insufficient.

honest.why: A 12-digit UPC-A whose GS1 mod-10 check digit validates (recomputed: 4, published: 4), published as gtin12 and mirrored into mpn and the variant barcode. This resolves outside the store.

storeLocal.verdict: a store-local id, accepted as an external one
storeLocal.why: The same value appears in 11 different fields on this page, among them Shopify's own `productId` and `data-product-id`, and alongside `gid://shopify/Product/8079462006899`. It is the store's internal product id, written into `mpn` by the theme. The store's real SKU is a different string entirely.

storeLocal.verdict: a store-local id, accepted as an external one
storeLocal.why: The same six digits are published as BOTH `sku` and `mpn`, adjacent in one JSON-LD object. A SKU is the store's own part number — the requirement's own insufficient-evidence list names it — so copying it into `mpn` cannot make it resolve anywhere else.
